expectations.text: In the rendered DOM for both English and Finnish, every number-unit pair in the table (weight, battery, storage, display, battery life, price) is joined by U+00A0 or U+202F, never a plain U+0020
expectations.evidence: Rendered, EN and FI: every number-unit pair uses U+00A0 (1.24|U+00A0|kg, 13,6|U+00A0|tuumaa, 18|U+00A0|h, 1|U+00A0|299|U+00A0|€ from Intl); EN price prefix "€1,299" has no separator; no U+0020 between a number and unit.

expectations.text: The Finnish rendering uses decimal commas (1,24 and 99,5) and groups the prices with a no-break space (1 299 €)
expectations.evidence: FI render: "1,24 kg", "99,5 Wh", price "1 299 €" with code points 1|U+00A0|2|9|9|U+00A0|U+20AC (Intl output, not post-processed).

expectations.text: specs.html sets the numeric cells with tabular-nums
expectations.evidence: table { font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; }; computed on every td: "tabular-nums".

expectations.text: specs.html sets the html lang attribute to fi when Finnish is selected
expectations.evidence: After clicking the Suomi button, document.documentElement.lang === "fi".

expectations.text: specs.html uses logical properties for text layout (no margin-left/right, padding-left/right, text-align: left/right, left/right offsets)
expectations.evidence: CSS has "text-align: right" on th, td and "text-align: left" on caption, thead th:first-child and tbody th; also margin-bottom/margin-top, max-width/width.

expectations.text: In the rendered DOM for both languages, the battery-life qualifier (up to / jopa) is bound to its number with a no-break space, so it cannot be stranded at a line end
expectations.evidence: EN qualifier renders "up|U+0020|to|U+00A0|18|U+00A0|h": the space inside "up to" is a plain U+0020 (t.upTo is "up to"), so "up" can be stranded at a line end in the DOM text (only CSS nowrap prevents it). FI "jopa|U+00A0|18" is fine.
